# Adult-onset Still disease

*Categories: Clinical knowledge > Internal medicine > Rheumatology and immunology > Myopathies and pain syndromes > Adult-onset Still disease*

[Original Article Link](/library/Zu0Zp3)

---

## Summary

Adult-onset <u>Still disease</u> (<u>AOSD</u>) is a rare inflammatory disorder characterized by <u>intermittent fever</u>, salmon-pink <u>rash</u>, symmetrical <u>polyarthritis</u>, and <u>arthralgia</u>. <u>AOSD</u> and <u>systemic juvenile idiopathic arthritis</u> are increasingly viewed as the same condition with different ages of onset due to their shared clinical features and laboratory findings. The exact cause is unknown. Life-threatening complications include <u>macrophage activation syndrome</u> and <u>fulminant hepatitis</u>. In patients with suggestive clinical features and laboratory findings (e.g., <u>leukocytosis</u> with <u>neutrophilia</u>, elevated <u>ferritin</u> levels), a comprehensive workup is needed to exclude alternative diagnoses (e.g., infections, autoimmune diseases, <u>malignancy</u>). Imaging studies (e.g., <u>echocardiography</u>, <u>high-resolution CT</u> chest) may be performed to assess for organ involvement. Prompt treatment with <u>biologic DMARDs</u> (e.g., <u>anakinra</u>) can prevent disease progression. A combination of <u>biologic DMARDs</u> and high-dose <u>glucocorticoids</u> are used in severe disease.

---

## Clinical features

* Disease presentation: variable

* Single or recurrent episodes

* Chronic, progressive disease

* Main features [[1]](/library/bmdHVq0)[[2]](/library/YmdnVq0)

* <u>Intermittent fever</u>: â¥ 39Â°C (â¥ 102.2Â°F) for > 7 days

* <u>Evanescent rash</u>

* <u>Erythematous</u> (salmon-pink) with <u>macules</u> and <u>papules</u>   [[2]](/library/YmdnVq0)

* Usually intermittent, coinciding with <u>fever</u>

* Typically on the trunk or <u>proximal</u> limbs

* Symmetrical <u>polyarthritis</u> (not always present), <u>arthralgias</u>, and/or <u>myalgias</u> [[1]](/library/bmdHVq0)[[2]](/library/YmdnVq0)

* Additional features [[1]](/library/bmdHVq0)[[2]](/library/YmdnVq0)

* <u>Sore throat</u>

* <u>Lymphadenopathy</u>

* <u>Serositis</u> (e.g., <u>pleural effusion</u>, <u>pericarditis</u>)

* <u>Splenomegaly</u>, <u>hepatomegaly</u>

* <u>Fulminant hepatitis</u> (in severe cases)

* Associated <u>interstitial lung disease</u>: <u>cough</u>, <u>dyspnea</u>, <u>clubbing</u>

## Diagnosis

### General principles [[1]](/library/bmdHVq0)[[2]](/library/YmdnVq0)




* Early referral to a specialist (e.g., rheumatology) is required for all patients with suspected <u>AOSD</u>.

* Diagnosis is based on:

* Suggestive clinical features and laboratory findings

* Exclusion of alternative diagnoses

* The <u>Yamaguchi classification criteria</u> may be used to support the diagnosis.





### <u>Laboratory studies</u> [[1]](/library/bmdHVq0)[[2]](/library/YmdnVq0)




* <u>CBC</u>: <u>Leukocytosis</u> with <u>neutrophilia</u> and <u>thrombocytosis</u> support the diagnosis; <u>leukopenia</u> suggests <u>macrophage activation syndrome</u>.

* <u>Inflammatory markers</u>: ↑↑↑ <u>ferritin</u>, ↑ <u>CRP</u>, ↑ <u>ESR</u>   [[2]](/library/YmdnVq0)

* <u>CMP</u>: ↑ <u>BUN</u>, ↑ <u>creatinine</u>

* <u>Liver chemistries</u>: ↑ <u>AST</u>, ↑ <u>ALT</u>

* <u>Coagulation studies</u>: ↑ <u>PT</u>, ↑ <u>D-dimer</u>, ↓ <u>fibrinogen</u>

* Other: ↑ CK, ↑ <u>LDH</u>

* Additional studies may be obtained to exclude alternative diagnoses in consultation with specialists.

* <u>Blood culture</u>, viral <u>serology</u> (e.g., <u>EBV</u>, <u>HIV</u>, <u>CMV</u>): to exclude infectious diseases

* <u>ANA</u>, <u>rheumatoid factor</u>, <u>ANCAs</u>: to exclude autoimmune conditions (e.g., <u>SLE</u>, <u>rheumatoid arthritis</u>, <u>polyarteritis nodosa</u>)

* <u>Bone marrow</u> or <u>lymph node</u> <u>biopsy</u>: if hematologic <u>malignancy</u> (e.g., <u>non-Hodgkin lymphoma</u>) is suspected





> [!WARNING]
> <u>Macrophage activation syndrome</u> should be suspected in patients with <u>AOSD</u> or <u>systemic juvenile idiopathic arthritis</u> and a normal or decreased <u>WBC count</u>, falling <u>ESR</u>, and/or increasing <u>triglyceride</u> levels.




### Imaging studies [[1]](/library/bmdHVq0)[[2]](/library/YmdnVq0)




* <u>X-ray</u> or <u>ultrasound</u> of affected <u>joints</u>: no specific findings but can help rule out <u>seronegative rheumatoid arthritis</u> [[3]](/library/j5d_Pq0)

* <u>Echocardiography</u>: if cardiopulmonary involvement (e.g., <u>pulmonary hypertension</u>, <u>myocarditis</u>) is suspected

* <u>High-resolution CT</u> chest: if pulmonary involvement is suspected

* CT chest, abdomen, and <u>pelvis</u>: if <u>malignancy</u> is suspected





### Classification criteria [[1]](/library/bmdHVq0)[[4]](/library/dLdo9q0)




The Yamaguchi criteria for AOSD are the most widely used criteria; ≥ 5 criteria must be fulfilled, including ≥ 2 major criteria.




* Major criteria

* <u>Fever</u> (â¥ 39Â°C) every day for ≥ 1 week

* <u>Arthralgia</u> and/or <u>arthritis</u> for ≥ 2 weeks

* Nonpruritic salmon-colored <u>rash</u> with <u>macules</u> and <u>papules</u> on the trunk or extremities

* <u>Leukocytosis</u> â¥ 10,000/mmÂ³ with ≥ 80% <u>neutrophils</u>

* Minor criteria

* <u>Pharyngitis</u> and/or <u>sore throat</u>

* <u>Lymphadenopathy</u> and/or <u>splenomegaly</u>

* Elevated <u>AST</u>, <u>ALT</u>, and/or <u>LDH</u>

* Negative <u>ANA</u> and <u>rheumatoid factor</u> (excludes other diagnoses)





> [!TIP]
> The <u>Yamaguchi classification criteria</u> generally have high <u>specificity</u> and <u>sensitivity</u>, but <u>sensitivity</u> can drop significantly if exclusion criteria are applied strictly. They aim to standardize case definitions for enrollment in clinical trials, not to guide practice. [[1]](/library/bmdHVq0)[[4]](/library/dLdo9q0)[[5]](/library/yRVdp80)
